problem_summary.summary: Find the area of the largest all-'1' square contained in a binary character matrix.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an m by n matrix of characters '0' and '1'. Return the maximum square area, or zero when no '1' exists.

brute_force.explanation: For every top-left cell, try each square size that stays within the matrix and inspect all cells in that square. Keep the largest size containing only '1' characters. This direct enumeration is practical only for small matrices.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every all-one square has a top-left coordinate and a side length considered by the loops. Inspecting its cells verifies whether it is valid, so the largest valid candidate is found.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(mnq^3) as a worst-case upper bound, where q = min(m,n): each top-left position can test O(q) side lengths and inspect O(q^2) cells per square.

optimized.explanation: For each cell treated as a square's bottom-right corner, store the largest all-one square side ending there. If the cell is '1', its side is one plus the minimum of the top, left, and top-left diagonal side lengths. Use one row of DP values and preserve the previous diagonal value while scanning left to right.
optimized.correctness_idea: A square of side s ending at the current cell requires a side-(s-1) square above, left, and diagonally up-left. The minimum of those three neighboring maximum sides is exactly the largest extendable interior, so the recurrence computes the maximum side for each endpoint.
optimized.time_complexity: O(mn), processing each matrix cell once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary space for one rolling DP row and its zero sentinel.
